function: Learned beam hopping for two neighboring LEO satellites: each beam agent picks which cell to illuminate per slot to maximize throughput, without intersatellite communication (pp. 6-8).
system: Two LEO satellites at 550 km, four beams each, 19 cells per satellite, single-antenna cells, 20 GHz, 500 MHz bandwidth, no RIS (pp. 3, 9).
method: Multiagent reinforcement learning: one independent DQN per beam (3 hidden layers, 128 neurons), shared global reward, offline training and onboard inference; non-learned Kalman filter predicts demand (pp. 7-9).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician fading with Nakagami-m parameters from elevation angle (model of [20]), free-space path loss, simulated time-correlated traffic; no standard channel model or dataset (pp. 3, 9).
test_conditions: Offline training, 7000 episodes; evaluation averages 500 test results; total demand swept 1300-2800 Mb/s and 4-64 satellites; no unseen-scenario test stated (pp. 9-13).
baselines: Non-learned: genetic-algorithm beam hopping (KA-GBH, NK-GBH) and random hopping; learned: only the proposed method without Kalman prediction (NK-GIRL-BH) and a centralized variant (CCEC) (pp. 9, 12-13).
metrics: System throughput (Mb/s), average packet queuing delay (ms), demand prediction error, training reward, processing time, beam conflict frequency (pp. 9-14).
complexity: Order of complexity O(J lth^3 sigma^2) + O(sum Wl-1 Wl sigma^2) per decision and processing time 237 us, compared with genetic algorithm schemes (Table II, p. 12).
q1_support: p. 3: "Based on this feature, we utilize the Rice fading model" in a custom simulator (elevation-dependent Rician and Nakagami-m parameters from [20], free-space path loss, simulated traffic on p. 9); no 3GPP TR 38.811 or other standard model and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 13: "we extended the original simulation" to 4-64 satellites, comparing PDCS and CCEC at each scale; the paper never states that a model trained on one setting was tested on an unseen one, and training is done per group on the ground.
q3_support: p. 9: "Learning Without Kalman Filter Prediction (NK-GIRL-BH):" is the proposed method minus a module (ablation), and CCEC on p. 13 is a centralized variant; KA-GBH, NK-GBH and Random are non-learned; no earlier learned beam-hopping method or standard learned baseline is compared.
q4_support: p. 12: "Table II summarizes the algorithmic complexity and processing time" of the schemes; the proposed method has O(J lth^3 sigma^2) + O(sum Wl-1 Wl sigma^2) and about 237 us per decision.
q5_support: p. 9: "The simulation is conducted on the Python 3.6 platform," with its own simulator and simulated traffic; no code or data link and no availability statement appear anywhere in the paper.
notes: Area: beam hopping of LEO satellites learned with multiagent DQN is beam control of a satellite link, so area 6; in satellite links beam scheduling counts as physical layer (Step 1, item 4). The Kalman-filter demand prediction is not learned. q1: the elevation-dependent Rician and Nakagami-m parameters follow the land mobile satellite model of Abdi et al. [20], a published statistical model and not 3GPP TR 38.811 or another standard; reviewer to confirm. q3: NK-GIRL-BH is an ablation and CCEC a centralized variant, so no earlier or standard learned baseline, though non-learned baselines exist. q4: Table II gives complexity orders and processing time.
